construct.name: cross-framework cellular automaton transition equivalence and runtime scaling
construct.intended_use: Provide a portable, trace-driven forest-fire workload and exact Rust reference before adding external framework adapters.
construct.claim_ceiling: Tier 1 Rust reference workload only; no cross-framework speed ranking or general ABM engine superiority claim.

units.resampling_unit: predeclared seed; grid sizes share the same seed and event-tape prefix
units.independent_unit: 20 fixed seed groups, each paired across 32×32 and 64×64 grid sizes
units.dependence_statement: The two grid-size runs for a given seed share the deterministic event-tape prefix and are paired. Ticks within a trajectory are serially dependent. No population inference or confidence interval is claimed.

sources.missingness_semantics: All state cells and event-tape positions are explicitly encoded. Missing tape words or cells fail validation; absent values are never interpreted as zero.

evaluation_distribution.sampling_frame: 20 predeclared seeds crossed with two grid sizes (32×32 and 64×64), 40 ticks and a synchronous fixed-boundary Moore-neighborhood forest-fire transition.

factors.weight_interpretation: Equal designed workload coverage, not prevalence.
Predeclared common-random-number blocks; each seed is paired across both grid sizes.

perturbation_families.rationale: Scheduler order is part of the model semantics; an in-place port can ignite cells one tick earlier than a double-buffer port.
perturbation_families.validity_check: Compare every per-tick state count and trajectory fingerprint against the synchronous reference.
expected_invariants: All cells read the previous complete grid during a tick.
Newly burning cells may only ignite neighbors on the next tick.
A sequential/in-place port must not be ranked as equivalent if trajectories differ.
perturbation_families.seed_policy: All adapters consume the exact same precomputed initial state and u16 event-tape words.

perturbation_families.rationale: Framework-native random generators would confound model/runtime comparison with RNG implementation.
perturbation_families.validity_check: Adapters must report input tape digest and consume exactly one event word per cell per tick.
expected_invariants: The event tape is generated outside the timed stepping loop.
All frameworks consume identical initial state and tape bytes.
Tape omission, reordering or replacement fails input conformance.
perturbation_families.seed_policy: SplitMix64 generator and stream separation are specified by the versioned reference implementation.

replication_design.independent_unit: Fixed seed-level initial state and common-random-number event-tape stream; two grid sizes per seed form a paired block.
replication_design.dependence_assessment: Twenty deterministic seed blocks provide coverage of software transition paths, not a random sample from a real-world fire process. Ticks are serially dependent; grid-size records are paired by seed.
replication_design.sample_size_rationale: Twenty fixed seeds × two grid sizes establish a reproducible conformance workload. No confidence interval, hazard prevalence or population inference is claimed.

metrics.aggregation: empty/tree/burning/ash counts at every tick, retained separately
empty + tree + burning + ash minus width × height at each tick
fingerprint of the ordered per-tick state-count trajectory; cross-framework ports must additionally be checked against exact per-cell state where available
time spent in Rust reference stepping after input/tape generation; startup and serialization are outside this timing
metrics.uncertainty_method: raw per-run only; no cross-framework claim

metrics.aggregation: fingerprint of row-major, tick-major u16 event tape; binary artifact SHA-256 is also emitted by CI

baselines.description: Rust implementation reads the complete prior grid and writes a separate next grid for every tick.
A fixture with a forced burning cell and zero ignition threshold; all new tree ignitions must be absent.

negative_controls.intervention: Change one framework adapter from synchronous double-buffer to sequential in-place mutation.
negative_controls.expected_result: Per-tick state trajectories/fingerprints differ; adapter is marked non-equivalent and excluded from runtime ranking.

negative_controls.intervention: Replace supplied event tape with framework-native RNG inside the stepping loop.
negative_controls.expected_result: Input tape fingerprint/conformance fails; no direct timing comparison is allowed.
Scenario validation fails closed with a tape-length mismatch.

negative_controls.intervention: Force one initial burning cell and set ignition threshold to zero.
negative_controls.expected_result: The initial fire becomes ash and no new burning cells appear after tick one.

holdouts.leakage_control: No external framework timing is claimed in this reference PR; future adapters must consume the same frozen tape bundle and pass exact equivalence before any performance ranking.

reproduction.runtime_environment: Rust edition 2024; exact-head GitHub Actions workflow; runtime diagnostics only for Rust reference
reproduction.humanity_atlas_run_artifact_ref: Not a Humanity Atlas civilizational scenario; benchmark workload and output receipts are produced by the engine comparison CI.

claim_report.claim_ceiling: Tier 1 Rust reference workload only; no cross-framework speed ranking or general ABM engine superiority claim.
known_limitations: No external framework adapter is implemented in this version.
FNV fingerprints are non-cryptographic fast checks; CI computes SHA-256 for the binary and CSV artifacts.
The synthetic fire process is a software workload, not an empirically calibrated fire-spread model.
Runtime measurements exclude startup/JIT, tape generation and serialization.
unsupported_strata: Agents.jl, Mesa, mesa-frames, NetLogo, MASON, Ark.jl and BAM Engine performance comparisons remain unrun.
No natural fire regimes, ecological calibration or real-world hazard claims.

components.notes: Synthetic oracle or explicit deterministic controller; not a human or LLM.
Stable serial execution in declared input order.
Reject invalid or out-of-contract inputs; no silent repair.
Capture every declared input, step, output and metric; missing records fail closed.
No unseeded random source is used by this deterministic fixture.

scheduler_policy.update_order: stable declared fixture order; deterministic serial execution
scheduler_policy.tie_breaking_rule: stable identifier then stable input index

exposure_policy.eligibility_rule: not applicable to this deterministic reference fixture
exposure_policy.state_visibility: all declared synthetic inputs are visible to the benchmark runner
